ety.text: Borrowed from English antielectron. By surface analysis, анти- (anti-) + электро́н (elektrón).

s.g: to doggedly pursue, to persistently seek or strive for

ety.text: From живо́тно- (živótno-) + deverbal from води́ть (vodítʹ, “to lead, to drive, to breed”).

s.g: Zhukov (a town in Kaluga Oblast, Russia, named after Georgy Zhukov)
to start to fear, to become afraid
reserve, store, supply, stock, stockpile, inventory, log, margin
(historical) zindan (an improvised cell consisting of a hole in the ground covered with a metal grille)
any improvised earth prison during the two Chechen wars, and during the Russo-Ukrainian War in the territories occupied by Russia.

ety.text: Borrowed from Classical Persian زِنْدَان (zindān) and/or Ottoman Turkish زندان (zindan).

s.g: elephant seal (mammal of the genus Mirounga)
being impatient (in anticipation of something), hard to bear, hard to be patient, hard to wait

x: Анто́н вы́шел, обёрнутый в полоте́нце, нали́л рю́мку во́дки и опроки́нул в себя́, как роднико́вую во́ду.

s.g: intended for beating back (a blow) (of a weapon)
beaten (made by beating, softened by beating, e.g. meat)

ety.text: Inherited from Old East Slavic папьрть (papĭrtĭ), from Proto-Slavic *papьrtь, from *pa- + *pьrtь (“front”). Cognate with Old Church Slavonic папръть (paprŭtĭ), Bulgarian папрът (paprăt).

x: Варва́ра поверте́ла в рука́х письмо́ и, не распеча́тывая, протяну́ла его́ Передо́нову.
Мне кажется порою, что солдаты, С кровавых не пришедшие полей, Не в землю нашу полегли когда-то, А превратились в белых журавлей.

s.g: to foresee, to envisage, to anticipate

ety.text: From German provozieren, itself derived from Latin provocare.

x: На восто́ке мо́жно бы́ло различи́ть в лёгком тума́не оста́вшийся уже́ позади́ мыс При́нца Уэ́льского.

s.g: to cleave, to split, to crack
to start talking, to tell/reveal/disclose the truth, to blab, to let it out, to spill the beans, to spill
Federal Service for Environmental, Technological and Nuclear Supervision

ety.text: From Latin Sīrius, from Ancient Greek Σείριος (Seírios), usually taken from σείριος (seírios, “scorching; scorcher”).

s.g: a rude and uncultured man from the military
a military officer whose interests and experience are strongly limited by his professional knowledge

x: Оста́вив у неё чемода́н, но взяв с собо́ю рюкза́к, где бы́ло ко́е-что́ из съестно́го, Воропа́ев вы́шел из особняка́.

ety.text: Substantivized neuter of съестно́й (sʺjestnój, “food”), from съесть (sʺjestʹ, “to eat up”) + -ной (-noj).

ety.text: Inherited from Old East Slavic топере (topere), itself inherited from Proto-Slavic *topьrvo. First recorded in Russian as тепе́речи (tepéreči) in 1562.

s.g: to conceal, to keep to oneself, to keep a secret

ety.text: From хи́трый (xítryj) + -о (-o) (stem-stressed variant) or from хи́трый (xítryj) + -о́ (-ó) (ending-stressed variant).
Ultimately from Tibetan གཡག (g.yag), from Proto-Sino-Tibetan *g-jak ~ g-jaŋ.
